name: Platform verification limitations and fair account-integrity review

attribution.legal_posture: First-party platform documentation describes controls and limitations; provider observations and source-attributed investigations supply context, while incident disclosure, identity finding, nationality assessment, court finding, labor-market prevalence and independently validated efficacy require separate sources. Verification remains a bounded process rather than a conclusive determination.

caveats: Avoid claims about unnamed accounts or platform prevalence.
Identity-verification limitations and location-only anomalies call for human review; DPRK affiliation requires corroborating evidence.
Identity-document imagery, synthetic-image examples, biometric templates, candidate-level telemetry, and raw graph nodes stay out of publication and operational use.

Identity documents, selfies, liveness recordings, addresses, phone numbers, emails, tax records, payment details, credentials, device identifiers, IP addresses, and raw screening reports stay unreproduced.
Platform-wide fraud metrics describe platform-wide activity; DPRK estimates require separate measurement.
Keep fake-interview malware separate from fraudulent employment unless a first-party source establishes the overlap.
Keep historical North Korea platform access distinct from a DPRK IT-worker attribution.
Face, accent, language, nationality, travel, time zone, VPN use, location mismatch, and payment-method change require corroboration before an adverse conclusion.
Facial comparison, accent, nationality, and travel heuristics are contextual signals requiring corroboration.
Identity or attribution requires more than a single face, image, document, VPN, location, device, network, profile, résumé, repository, contact, or behavior signal.
Payment-beneficiary review remains private and compliance-led; sensitive financial selectors are excluded from the public dataset.
A persona is a reported platform identity, while legal identity and platform verification remain separate questions.
Platform controls, restrictions, and verification outcomes are review inputs; DPRK affiliation, legal identity, nationality, work location, and sole-operator control require corroborating evidence.
Publish limitations adjacent to control descriptions.
Publish provider-level controls and limitations; private account-level evidence remains outside the record.

Retain only minimal control decisions and provenance; people, personas, accounts, entities, private profiles, payment identifiers, addresses, credentials, images, and raw screening artifacts stay outside the record.
Sanctions, employment, criminal, and identity checks have jurisdictional and methodological limits; document exactly what was checked and when.

Successful or failed verification is one bounded observation; legal identity, nationality, DPRK affiliation, worker continuity, present account control and product-wide performance require separate evidence.
Use explainable multi-signal review, minimization, bounded retention, trained human adjudication, correction, appeal, accessibility accommodations, and applicable legal review.

Use multiple explainable signals, proportional human review, correction, and appeal; face, accent, language, nationality, travel, time zone, VPN use, location mismatch, or payment change alone are insufficient for adverse decisions.
Use multiple independently explainable signals, human review, proportionality, correction, and appeal.

statements: Fiverr combines identity evidence, selfie/liveness matching, region consistency, account-integrity review, and enforcement for concealed identity/location or multiple accounts. Crucially, Fiverr says verification depends on user-supplied information and cannot guarantee every verified freelancer is who they claim to be, and says routine travel or logging in from different places alone does not trigger a flag.
limitations: Publish limitations adjacent to control descriptions.
No facial comparison, accent, nationality, or travel heuristic should be used independently.
Avoid claims about unnamed accounts or platform prevalence.
Identity-verification limitations and location-only anomalies require human review and cannot establish DPRK affiliation.

Platform controls, restrictions, and verification outcomes are review inputs; none independently proves or excludes DPRK affiliation, legal identity, nationality, work location, or sole operator control.

Use multiple explainable signals, proportional human review, correction, and appeal; do not make adverse decisions from face, accent, language, nationality, travel, time zone, VPN use, location mismatch, or payment change alone.

Retain only minimal control decisions and provenance. No people, personas, accounts, entities, private profiles, payment identifiers, addresses, credentials, images, or raw screening artifacts are included.
Persona is not legal identity, and platform verification is not legal attribution.
No adverse conclusion may rest on face, accent, language, nationality, travel, time zone, VPN use, location mismatch, or payment-method change alone.
Use multiple independently explainable signals, human review, proportionality, correction, and appeal.
Publish provider-level controls and limitations, not private account-level evidence.

Do not reproduce identity documents, selfies, liveness recordings, addresses, phone numbers, emails, tax records, payment details, credentials, device identifiers, IP addresses, or raw screening reports.
Do not turn platform-wide fraud metrics into DPRK estimates.
Keep historical North Korea platform access distinct from a DPRK IT-worker attribution.
Keep fake-interview malware separate from fraudulent employment unless a first-party source establishes the overlap.
Sanctions, employment, criminal, and identity checks have jurisdictional and methodological limits; document exactly what was checked and when.
Payment-beneficiary review should remain private and compliance-led; no sensitive financial selector belongs in the public dataset.

sources.support: GitLab reports just-over-40-percent success across one observed operation's attempts to obtain enhanced verification on unnamed professional networking services. This source-reported result is a bounded point-in-time observation, not proof of legal identity or worker continuity. Evidence boundary: GitLab's source-attributed investigation, not a court finding. The platform being verified is not named in the relevant claim, the attempt count and decision criteria are not disclosed, and successful platform verification does not establish civil identity, worker continuity, present account control, or product-wide failure rate
sources.locator: Case Study 3: synthetic identity construction workflow, verification-status field, aggregate success result, implications and mitigations; Case Study 4: payment-processor rotation and facilitator/device-access observations

sources.support: Fiverr may require an original government ID, selfie authenticity and matching, correct region selection, and no active VPN during verification. It also warns that verification relies on user-supplied information and cannot guarantee every verified freelancer is who they claim to be. Publish the explicit limitation alongside the controls. Never use face, language, VPN use, or location alone as an attribution signal. Fiverr combines identity evidence, selfie/liveness matching, region consistency, account-integrity review, and enforcement for concealed identity/location or multiple accounts. Crucially, Fiverr says verification depends on user-supplied information and cannot guarantee every verified freelancer is who they claim to be, and says routine travel or logging in from different places alone does not trigger a flag
sources.locator: ID verification Step by step; How we use your data; ID verified freelancers; FAQs

sources.support: Fiverr says accounts can lose selling eligibility for multiple accounts, concealed identity or location, or activity previously associated with fraud, while noting that ordinary travel or multiple login locations alone do not trigger a flag. Preserve the negative: travel or multiple locations alone are not a valid adverse conclusion. Fiverr combines identity evidence, selfie/liveness matching, region consistency, account-integrity review, and enforcement for concealed identity/location or multiple accounts. Crucially, Fiverr says verification depends on user-supplied information and cannot guarantee every verified freelancer is who they claim to be, and says routine travel or logging in from different places alone does not trigger a flag

sources.support: Pindrop reports at least two source-labeled suspected cases in which synthetic imagery passed document verification. Evidence boundary: Provider-reported observations from Pindrop's own pipeline. The article does not publish methodology sufficient to reproduce its labels, cohort sizes for every percentage, independent validation, named candidates, legal identities, or a labor-market prevalence estimate. Its 'confirmed fraud' and 'linked to North Korea' labels are source labels, not adjudications
